notes.readingWpm: Silent reading of non-fiction, adults: Brysbaert (2019) meta-analysis of 190 studies.
notes.transcribeWpm: Average of 168,000 people typing online: Dhakal et al. (CHI 2018), reported as 52 wpm.
notes.composeWpm: Composing is slower than copying because you think while you type. Derived: 52 wpm x 0.58, the composing-to-copying ratio Karat et al. measured (19 / 32.5). Edit this if you have your own number.
notes.klm: Keystroke-Level Model operator times (Card, Moran & Newell). K set to 0.2 s, a 52 wpm typist (60 / (52 x 5 characters) = 0.23 s, rounded toward the model's skilled band).
notes.writing: Writing is planning, drafting and reviewing (Hayes & Flower's model of the writing process). Drafting uses composeWpm. Planning is an assumption: 45 s to decide what a short reply says, 4 min to outline a one-pager. Refining is re-reading the draft twice at readingWpm and retyping about 20% of it at transcribeWpm (assumption).
